When our president and senators are sworn in to their positions they take an oath to uphold the Constitution. In the Constitution Article II, Section 2, authorizes the president to nominate a number of federal positions (including members of the Supreme Court) and charges the Senate with giving "advice and consent." While we often don't agree with our elected officials regarding the implementation of their oaths, to do nothing is not an option designated to them by our Founding Fathers. Now that our president has nominated a qualified jurist, the Senate is mandated to fulfill their Constitutional duty. If they don't like him, they can not approve him. If they don't like him they can advise the President as to what qualities the nominee should have, but James Madison and his colleagues did not authorize the Senate to ignore the President's nominee.
